The Anambra State Police Command has arrested five suspects in connection with the kidnap and murder of a man identified as Chinedu Echezona, recovering his remains, vehicle and N5m ransom allegedly collected by the suspects. The suspects were arrested on November 12, 2026, at Omoba Phase II, Nkpor, Onitsha, following sustained intelligence-led investigations by operatives of the Rapid Response Squad, Awkuzu. The state Police Public Relations Officer, SP Tochukwu Ikenga, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday, saying the victim was kidnapped in the early hours of January 29, 2026. According to Ikenga, the kidnappers initially demanded a ransom of N20m, while efforts by the police to unravel the circumstances surrounding the abduction, including investigations that extended to a neighbouring state, did not initially yield a breakthrough. He said the suspects were identified as Chidozie Francis, 24; Kosisọchukwu Eziani, 28; Akachukwu Maduabuchi, 22; Chibuzor Onurah, 29; and Echezona Ude, 22. Initial investigative efforts, which extended to a neighbouring state, did not yield the desired breakthrough, as the armed gang reportedly demanded a ransom of N20 million.” He said the suspects allegedly confessed during interrogation to their involvement in the crime, adding that they admitted abducting Echezona and collecting N5m ransom. According to the police spokesman, the suspects further allegedly confessed to killing the victim after collecting the ransom and disclosed that two firearms were used in the operation. 2027: Keep politics out of churches, Soludo tells politicians Gunmen shoot driver, abduct three passengers in Benue Police arrest five over kidnap, murder, recover N5m ransom in Anambra Ikenga said the victim’s remains were recovered at about noon on November 14 after operatives, acting on information obtained from the suspects, took them to the location where the remains had allegedly been concealed. He added that the remains had been deposited in a mortuary for preservation and forensic examination. The police spokesman said the victim’s black Honda CR-V Jeep, with registration number YAB 220 DM, and the N5m ransom allegedly collected by the suspects were also recovered. Meanwhile, the Commissioner of Police, CP Nnanna Oji Ama, has directed the operatives to intensify efforts to recover the two firearms allegedly used in the crime and establish the full circumstances surrounding the incident. Ama commended the operatives for their persistence and professionalism, particularly for ensuring that the case was not abandoned despite the considerable time that had elapsed since the victim’s abduction. The CP reiterated the command’s determination to pursue criminal elements, dismantle criminal networks and ensure that perpetrators of violent crimes are brought to justice. He also assured residents that the command would continue to deploy intelligence-driven policing strategies to protect lives and property across the state.
